Content:
Govt. Haraganga College (established on 18 Dec 1938) is one of the most esteemed educational institutions in Bangladesh. Over the decades, the college has produced thousands of graduates who are now contributing to society at national and international levels. The Govt. Haraganga College Alumni Association (hereinafter referred to as "HARAGANGIAN") unites former students of the institution under a shared commitment to lifelong connection, service, ethical conduct, and collective progress. This Constitution defines the governance, membership, responsibilities, and enduring vision of the Association. The Association shall operate in accordance with the principles set forth in this Constitution, including strict political neutrality.

Article I: Name, Nature & Motto

Section 1: Name
The official name of the organization shall be Govt. Haraganga College Alumni Association, also referred to as "HARAGANGIAN" for social platforms, cultural and informal representation only.

Section 2: Founding Date
The official founding date of the organization shall be 29 Nov 2025.

Section 3: Nature of the Association
The Association shall remain:
1. Non-political
2. Non-religious
3. Inclusive to all eligible alumni
4. Non-profit
5. Patron of Education and Culture
6. Philanthropic

Section 4: Motto
The official motto of the organization shall be "Sharing Heritage, Aligning Lives, Integrating Networks".

Section 5: Branding & Identity
The Association shall have the right to use the name "Govt. Haraganga College", its logo, and related branding only with formal written permission from the Institution. Unauthorized personal or commercial use is strictly prohibited. Such permission shall not imply ownership or institutional control unless expressly stated in writing.

Section 6: Logo
The official logo of the Govt. Haraganga College Alumni Association is a symbolic representation of the institution's heritage and the shared values of its graduates. The design elements are defined as follows:

Historic Heritage: The apex of the logo features a detailed rendering of the Govt. Haraganga College historic building, representing the foundation of the institution's academic legacy.

The Open Book: Located within the shield, it symbolizes lifelong learning, knowledge, and the primary mission of education.

The Torch: This quadrant represents enlightenment, leadership, and the guiding light that education provides to society.

The Graduation Cap (Mortarboard): This symbol marks the successful completion of academic journeys and the transition from student to alumnus.

The Handshake: Situated at the base of the shield, it signifies the unity, networking, and mutual support of the "Haragangian" community.

The Identity & Legacy: The surrounding red and gold border displays the official association name and its establishment year, Est. 2025.

Section 7: Flag
The official flag of the Alumni Association features a solid white background with the Association's logo positioned prominently in the centre. The white colour of the flag serves as a symbol of peace, harmony, non-violence, and purity.

Section 8: Theme Song
To be finalized by the Executive Committee.

Section 9: Registration No
To be finalized by the Executive Committee.

Section 10: Registered Office
The Registered Office of the Association shall be at an address to be finalized by the Executive Committee. This address shall be used for all legal correspondence until changed by the Executive Committee and notified to the Registrar of Societies.

Section 11: Banner and Signboard
To be finalized by the Executive Committee.

Section 12: Digital Data Platform
To be finalized by the Executive Committee.

Section 13: Social Media Platforms
The Association's social media platforms shall be finalized by the Executive Committee.

All undefined items under this Article shall be finalized by the Executive Committee through formal bylaws within 6 months of registration. Until such definitions are finalized, no interim use shall create legal or financial obligations for the Association.

Article II: Purpose & Objectives

1. To connect alumni through networking, reunions, and professional exchange.

2. To foster mutual support with ethical conduct.

3. To celebrate the Institution's legacy via cultural and academic events.

4. To promote social responsibility, philanthropy, and collective welfare, including but not limited to blood donation programs, tree plantation initiatives, counseling services, and humanitarian aid.

5. To ensure fair participation opportunities for all alumni.

6. To support official college programs (sports day, prize ceremonies etc).

7. To develop a Social & Recreational Centre.

8. To collaborate on student-focused educational and cultural programs.

9. To promote digital literacy, modern career training, and entrepreneurship among alumni and students.

10. To maintain a long-term archival project documenting alumni achievements and the Institution's history.

11. To provide financial assistance and scholarships to meritorious and financially disadvantaged students, subject to policies approved by the Executive Committee.

Article III: Membership

Section A: Eligibility & Verification
All ex-students (including previously enrolled or registered students) of Government Haraganga College are eligible.

Required proof: testimonial, certificate, transcript, or any verifiable official document.

Membership is subject to approval by the Executive Committee. Approval shall not be unreasonably withheld and must be based on documented eligibility criteria. The Association may deny or revoke membership for misconduct. Members must comply with this Constitution.

"Years since obtaining HSC Certification" shall be calculated from the date of the HSC passing year.

Former students who did not complete HSC but studied at least one academic year may apply for Associate Membership.

Section B: Membership Types
Voting Members (Paid): Founding, Executive, and General.

Non-Voting Members: Associate, Honorary, and Advisory.

Section C: Founding Membership
Eligibility:
- Must be a certified alumnus of the Institution.
- Must have completed at least 20 years since obtaining HSC Certification.
- Must be a Graduate (Bachelor Certified) from a recognized Institution.
- Outstanding contributions, clarified as either (a) a minimum defined donation slab set by bylaws, for which the Executive Committee shall publish clear thresholds annually, or (b) a major intellectual, developmental or technical contribution: a documented, legacy-defining contribution to the Institution demonstrating the strategic leadership necessary to uphold constitutional duties and decisively guide the Association's foundational vision, requiring formal documentation and ratification by a two-thirds majority vote of the Executive Committee.
- Demonstrated leadership.
- Clean disciplinary record.
- Must not hold active partisan political positions at local, national, or international levels.
- Should act as advisor or mentor.

Founding Members shall also be known and recognized as Lifetime Members of the Association.

Founding Members must submit a "Declaration of Non-Political Engagement" to maintain active status. Failure to submit results in automatic suspension until compliance.

Section D: Executive Membership
Eligibility:
- Must be a certified alumnus of the Institution.
- Must have completed at least 10 years since obtaining HSC Certification.
- Must be a Graduate (Bachelor Certified) from a recognized Institution.
- Active role in events and decision-making.
- Relevant skills preferred.
- Good moral standing.
- Must be a General Member in good standing.

Executive Members must attend at least 60% of committee meetings per term.

Section E: General Membership
Eligibility:
- Must be a certified alumnus of the Institution.
- Must have completed at least 5 years since obtaining HSC Certification.
- Interest in alumni activities.
- Payment of membership fee. Must be duly registered, with all applicable registration and annual fees paid and no outstanding dues.

General Members are voting members.

Section F: Associate Membership
Open to any verified ex-student, with no years-since-HSC requirement. A registration fee only is payable.

Associate Members are non-voting and their access is limited to open programs. They may join non-policy subcommittees (for example, event volunteer teams), and may upgrade to General Membership at any time by satisfying its conditions.

Section G: Honorary Membership
Honorary Membership is offered to distinguished contributors and requires two-thirds approval of the Executive Committee. Honorary Members are non-voting unless voting rights are specifically granted, and must not use their title for personal promotion.

Section H: Advisory Membership
1. Eligibility. Advisory Membership is for individuals who provide high-level guidance, institutional linkage, and community insight:
i. Principal of Govt. Haraganga College
ii. Vice Principal of the College
iii. Former Principals of Colleges
iv. Former Teachers of the College
v. Current Teachers of the College (selected rotationally or by recommendation)
vi. Alumni with exceptional contributions to society or community, who must meet at least two of the following criteria:
   a. Minimum 10 years of demonstrable service in social, educational, charitable, or developmental initiatives.
   b. Documented leadership roles in local, national, or international community organizations.
   c. Significant contributions to youth development, public welfare, education, or health campaigns.
   d. Recognized work (awards, citations, published achievements) that aligns with the Institution's values.
   e. Proven record of non-political, ethical community service positively impacting society.
vii. Advisory Members shall not be counted toward quorum requirements of the General Body or the Executive Committee.

2. Conditions:
- Advisory Members are non-voting.
- They cannot contest Executive Committee elections.
- They may attend meetings by invitation, provide recommendations, and advise the Executive Committee.
- No membership fee is required.
- Term: 3 years, renewable by Executive Committee approval.
- They must maintain neutrality and ethical conduct at all times.
- Advisory Members representing government or institutional posts shall not be counted as organizational members for quorum.

3. Roles & Responsibilities:
- Advise on long-term policy, institutional strategy, and major initiatives.
- Review annual reports, budgets, and proposals.
- Ensure the Association remains apolitical, inclusive, and ethical.
- Mediate in escalated disputes if requested by the Executive Committee.
- Act as a bridge between alumni, the College, and community stakeholders.

Section I: Membership Application & Approval
An applicant submits the membership form together with supporting documents. Verification is completed within 30 days, after which the Executive Committee approves or rejects the application. False information results in immediate termination. Rejected applicants may file an appeal within 15 working days.

Section J: Membership Terms
- Founding: Permanent / Lifetime, unless revoked.
- Executive: 3 years, renewable. May be upgraded to Lifetime status per Section C.
- General & Associate: Continuous.
- Honorary: Lifetime, or a term as approved.
- Advisory: 3-year term, renewable upon Executive Committee approval.

Section K: Member Rights & Responsibilities
Common rights and responsibilities: attend meetings and events; respectfully engage with members; uphold the Association's reputation and ethics; maintain confidentiality.

Tier-specific rights:
- Founding & Executive: full voting rights, eligible for Executive Committee elections, full facility access, must pay dues.
- General: voting rights, full facility access, must pay dues.
- Associate: non-voting, limited access.
- Honorary: as defined by the Executive Committee.
- Advisory: non-voting; may attend strategic and AGM meetings upon invitation; provide recommendations to the Executive Committee; cannot hold office in the Executive Committee; serve as institutional and community guidance.

Future Lifetime Members: the Executive Committee reserves the right to grant "Lifetime Membership" status to Executive Members in the future, based on significant donations, outstanding service, or other criteria as defined in the Bylaws.

Section L: Resignation & Register
Any member may resign by written notice to the General Secretary. The Association shall maintain a Membership Register containing each member's name, address, membership type, date of joining, and date of termination.

Article IV: Executive Committee

Section A: Composition & Term
The Executive Committee shall consist of 15 positions, comprising 13 elected positions and 2 ex-officio non-voting positions, for a term of three (3) years.

Section B: Founding Member Legacy Provision
To preserve institutional memory, three (3) of the thirteen (13) elected Executive Committee positions shall be filled by Founding Members for the first fifteen (15) years, after which this provision may be reviewed. This reservation shall not create hereditary or permanent entitlement beyond the period specified.

Section C: Transition Flexibility
If fewer than three eligible Founding Members contest the election in any cycle, the remaining positions shall be opened to eligible Executive Members for that cycle. If the quota cannot be met despite notifications, elections shall proceed without the quota for that cycle.

Section D: Positions & Duties
1. President - leads the organization and represents the Association.
2. Vice President - assists the President and assumes their duties when absent.
3. General Secretary - manages correspondence and records minutes.
4. Office Secretary - manages the office, documents, and centre operations.
5. Joint Secretary-1 - supports the General Secretary.
6. Joint Secretary-2 - supports the General Secretary.
7. Treasurer - manages finances and prepares reports.
8. Media, Cultural & Sports Secretary - plans cultural events and handles print and media.
9. Organizational Secretary - handles member engagement.
10. Information and Technology Secretary - manages the digital platform and database.
11. Member-1 - supports Executive Committee operations.
12. Member-2 - supports Executive Committee operations.
13. Law Secretary - constitutional and legislative activities.
14. Immediate Past President - non-voting advisor.
15. Institutional Representative - non-voting advisor; the current GHC Principal or Vice Principal.

Section E: Eligibility Clauses for Technical Positions
1. Law Secretary. The Law Secretary shall either have demonstrable contribution to the drafting, review, or interpretation of this Constitution or the Bylaws, or be a qualified legal professional or legal advisor with documented experience in constitutional, corporate, or organizational governance matters, including service as a legal or constitutional advisor to companies, institutions, or registered organizations.

2. Information and Technology Secretary. The Information and Technology Secretary must possess substantial hands-on professional experience in one or more of the following areas: software programming or application development; cybersecurity or information security management; database design, administration, or data governance; digital systems administration, platforms, or technology infrastructure. Relevant academic qualifications, professional certifications, or verifiable project experience shall be considered acceptable evidence.

Section F: Founding Member Representation within Elected Positions
1. Of the thirteen (13) elected Executive Committee positions, three (3) shall be reserved for Founding Member representation.
2. These three positions shall be the following named offices: President, General Secretary, and Treasurer.
3. Where multiple eligible Founding Members contest a reserved position, the position shall be filled by election through votes of the Voting Members.
4. Where only one eligible Founding Member contests a reserved position, that candidate shall be declared elected unopposed.
5. Where no eligible Founding Member contests a reserved position, the position shall be opened to other eligible Executive Members and filled through election.

Section G: Appointed / Ex-Officio Positions (Non-Voting)
1. Immediate Past President - non-voting advisor.
2. Institutional Representative - non-voting advisor; the current GHC Principal or Vice Principal.

Section H: Meetings
The Executive Committee must meet at least half-yearly with minutes archived. Quorum shall be 50% of elected members.

Section I: Succession
If any elected Executive Committee member resigns, passes away, or is incapacitated during their term, the Executive Committee may appoint a replacement from eligible members to serve until the next AGM.

Article V: Governance & Elections

Section A: Annual General Meeting (AGM)
The AGM is held once yearly for all members to discuss performance, activities, and budget.

Section B: Special Meetings
Special meetings can be called by the President or the Executive Committee when required.

Section C: Elections
Elections for the Executive Committee are held during the AGM every three years, and the process must ensure compliance with the Founding Member quota. Voting is conducted electronically, with alternatives if needed, by the Voting Members, and results are announced at the AGM.

Notice of elections and candidate nominations must be sent to all Voting Members at least 21 days prior to the AGM. Election Commission decisions are binding unless formally overturned by the AGM.

Section D: Candidacy for the Executive Committee
Automatic eligibility: Founding Members and Executive Members in good standing are automatically eligible to contest elections.

Special Nomination for General Members: a General Member may be nominated as a candidate through a Special Nomination, which requires a written proposal by at least two Executive Committee members; demonstration of exceptional, documented service to the Association over a minimum of one year; and approval by a two-thirds majority vote of the sitting Executive Committee.

All candidates must formally accept the nomination and confirm their willingness to serve if elected. If an Executive Committee position becomes vacant, the Executive Committee may fill it temporarily until the next AGM.

Section E: Election Commission
A three-member independent Election Commission shall be appointed by the Executive Committee 60 days before an election to administer a fair and neutral process. Election Commission members cannot be candidates in the election they oversee, and Executive Committee members cannot appoint relatives to the Commission. Election disputes are handled by the Appeal Panel. Commission decisions are binding unless overturned by the AGM.

Article VI: Financial Management

Section A: Bank Account
The bank account shall be opened in the official name of the Association with a recognized bank, and operated jointly by any two of the following three office bearers: President, General Secretary, and Treasurer.

Section B: Fundraising
Funds are raised through membership fees, donations, fundraising events, and merchandise sales.

Section C: Expenditures
Funds shall be allocated for events, educational support, community projects, Centre operations, administrative expenses, meetings, and digital platform maintenance, and to the following designated funds:

Educational Support Fund - for meritorious, financially disadvantaged current students.

Community Relief (Poor) Fund - for alumni and families facing severe verified hardship.

Social & Recreational Centre Fund - for the acquisition, maintenance, and operation of the Association's physical hub and assets, which will also serve as the Association's Office.

Separate accounts and records shall be maintained for designated funds.

Section D: Auditing & Transparency
The Treasurer presents the annual budget and report at the AGM. An annual internal audit and an independent audit shall be conducted at least once every financial year, or as required by law. All transactions require receipts. All bank transactions require two authorized signatures from the President, General Secretary, and Treasurer, or an Executive Committee-approved alternate. Audited financial statements shall be presented at every AGM.

Article VII: Code of Ethics & Conduct

Members and office bearers shall maintain the highest ethical standards; ensure inclusivity and non-discrimination; protect member confidentiality; uphold political and religious neutrality; operate with transparency; and disclose and manage conflicts of interest annually.

Political neutrality applies in particular to Founding Members, Executive Members, and Advisory Members representing public institutions.

Article VIII: Amendments to the Constitution

Amendments may be proposed by the Executive Committee or by petition of 20% of the Voting Members.

Ratification requires a two-thirds majority vote at a properly convened AGM.

Proposed amendments must be circulated to Voting Members at least 14 days before the AGM.

Article IX: Bylaws

Section 1: Governance
The Executive Committee may establish and amend Bylaws by a two-thirds vote, provided they do not conflict with this Constitution.

Section 2: Meetings
The AGM is held once yearly; special meetings require 7 days' notice.

Section 3: Elections
Elections are conducted every 3 years, and all Voting Members in good standing may vote.

Section 4: Financial Guidelines
No funds shall be used for political or personal purposes.

Section 5: Political Activities
The Association shall remain strictly non-political. No member shall use the name, platform, funds, or assets of the Association for political activities.

Article X: Disciplinary Procedures

Section 1: Grounds for Action
Misconduct, fraud, misuse of funds, violation of neutrality (for Founding and Executive Members), harassment, discrimination, or criminal conviction.

Section 2: Types of Action
Written warning, suspension, removal from committee, revocation of rights, or termination.

Section 3: Procedure
A written complaint is submitted to the Disciplinary Committee, as defined by the Executive Committee. An investigation follows, with the right of defense. The decision is taken by a two-thirds majority of the Executive Committee, and the judgment is documented.

Section 4: Appeal
A written appeal may be filed within 30 days to the Appeal Panel, whose decision is final.

Article XI: Interim Provisions

Section 1: Purpose of the Interim Executive Committee
The Interim Executive Committee (IEC) may also be referred to as the Convening Committee (CC) or Adhoc Committee (AC). Its purpose is to manage the Association's formation, prepare the Constitution, execute the legal documents necessary for registration, open bank accounts, and organize the First General Meeting and the subsequent First Executive Committee Election.

Section 2: Formation and Tenure
The initial Convening Committee shall select a temporary Interim Executive Committee, consisting of a President, General Secretary, and Treasurer, to manage legal processes. The IEC serves a temporary term which ends automatically upon the declaration of results for the First Executive Committee Election conducted under Article V.

Section 3: Powers and Limitations
The IEC has the limited authority to execute legal documents and submissions required for registration; to open bank accounts and manage administrative funds from initial fees and donations; to incur expenses strictly related to registration, office setup, and the inaugural election; and to coordinate all pre-election events and activities and the smooth transition culminating in the Executive Committee's assumption of office.

The IEC is strictly prohibited from entering into long-term contracts, initiating major projects, or amending this Constitution or the Digital Platform Structure.

Article XII: Dissolution of the Association

Section 1: Method of Dissolution
The Association may be dissolved only by a resolution passed at a Special General Meeting convened specifically for this purpose. The resolution must be approved by not less than three-fourths (75%) of the Voting Members present and voting.

Section 2: Notice of Dissolution Meeting
Notice of such a meeting, stating the terms of the proposed resolution, shall be sent to all members at least 30 days in advance.

Section 3: Winding Up Process
Upon passing the dissolution resolution, the Executive Committee shall act as the Winding-Up Committee or appoint one; all liabilities and obligations of the Association shall be discharged; and no member shall receive any personal benefit from the Association's assets.

Section 4: Disposal of Surplus Assets
After settling all debts and liabilities, any remaining assets shall not be distributed among members. They must be transferred to Govt. Haraganga College for educational or development purposes, or to another registered charitable organization with similar objectives, as determined by the Winding-Up Committee and approved by the final General Meeting.

Section 5: Final Returns
The Winding-Up Committee shall file all necessary dissolution documents with the relevant government authorities, such as the Registrar of Societies, as required by law.

Section 6: Cessation of Existence
The Association shall be considered dissolved upon completion of the winding-up process and receipt of formal confirmation from the relevant authorities. The dissolution resolution and the asset disposal report shall be submitted to the Registrar of Societies within 30 days.

Article XIII: Future Vision

A sustainable Educational Fund for underprivileged students.

Community Development initiatives.

Structured Career Mentorship & Training programs.

This Constitution was ratified to guide the Govt. Haraganga College Alumni Association (HARAGANGIAN).
